title: About
text: This project explores county-level demographic shifts across Florida between the 2000 and 2020 Decennial Censuses, focusing on changes in Hispanic, non-Hispanic White, Black, and Asian population shares.

title: About
text:
Data Source
Data is sourced from the U.S. Census Bureau decennial censuses (2000, 2010, and 2020) retrieved using the tidycensus package in R:

2000 & 2010: Summary File 1 (SF1)
2020: Public Law 94-171 Redistricting Data Summary File

title: About
text:
Tools & Packages

R & RStudio
Quarto for reproducible web publishing
Leaflet & sf for spatial data manipulation and interactive mapping
Tidyverse for data reshaping and analysis

This project was created by JMercado30 as part of data science coursework.

title: Florida Census Demographics (2000–2020)
text:
Between 2000 and 2020, Florida saw significant demographic shifts across all major racial and ethnic groups:

Hispanic: Substantial increases statewide, especially in central and southwest Florida.
White (non-Hispanic): Decreased as a overall percentage of population in almost all 67 counties.
Black: Steady population shares in northern counties, with growth in select central and southern metros.
Asian: Steady percentage growth across major suburban and university counties.

Use the radio buttons in the upper right to toggle which demographic shift colors the map. Hover over any county to view the 20-year shift for the selected group.
